brief: Our company coordinates ground-handling operations across several airports. Aircraft turnaround delays can affect crew availability, passenger connections, ground equipment, servicing tasks and departure slots. We want an intelligent system that identifies operational conflicts, evaluates recovery alternatives, coordinates authorized teams and maintains a complete decision trail. Safety-critical operations must remain subject to the appropriate operational authorities.

items.name: Turnaround

value.description: One aircraft turnaround at one airport: arrival-to-departure handling of a flight.

items.rationale: The brief is about aircraft turnaround delays across several airports. The turnaround is the natural unit of a case.

items.name: OperationalConflict

value.description: A detected conflict affecting a turnaround: crew availability, passenger connection, ground equipment, servicing task or departure slot.

items.rationale: The brief asks the system to identify operational conflicts and lists the five impacted areas.

items.name: RecoveryOption

value.description: An alternative for resolving a conflict, e.g. reassigning equipment, resequencing servicing or requesting a new slot.

items.rationale: The brief asks the system to evaluate recovery alternatives. The states support a human approval step before anything is executed.

items.name: TaskAssignment

value.description: A task given to an authorized team to carry out an approved recovery option.

items.rationale: The brief asks the system to coordinate authorized teams. The fields and states are my reading.

items.name: DecisionRecord

value.description: An entry in the decision trail: what was decided about a recovery option, by whom, when and why.

items.rationale: The brief asks the system to maintain a complete decision trail.
A turnaround can suffer several conflicts at once (crew, equipment, slot).
Several recovery alternatives are evaluated for each conflict.
Carrying out an approved option means coordinating one or more teams.
Each approval, rejection or escalation of an option is traced.

items.name: detect_conflict

value.description: Register an operational conflict on a turnaround from operational data and mark the turnaround disrupted.

items.rationale: The brief asks for identification of operational conflicts.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: evaluate_recovery_options

value.description: Produce and score recovery alternatives for a detected conflict.

items.rationale: The brief asks for evaluation of recovery alternatives. This step only produces proposals and changes nothing operationally.

items.name: submit_option_for_review

value.description: Send a proposed recovery option to the responsible person for a decision.

items.rationale: Recovery decisions belong to people. This action hands the option over to them.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: approve_recovery_option

value.description: An authorized person approves a recovery option.

items.rationale: The brief says operations stay with the appropriate authorities. Approval is a human decision.

items.name: reject_recovery_option

value.description: An authorized person rejects a recovery option.

items.rationale: This is the counterpart of approval and is needed for a complete decision trail.

items.name: record_decision

value.description: Write the decision on a recovery option (who, when, why) to the decision trail.

items.rationale: The brief asks for a complete decision trail.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: escalate_conflict

value.description: Escalate a conflict to the competent operational authority when it is safety-critical or cannot be resolved in time.

items.rationale: The brief says safety-critical operations must remain subject to operational authorities.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: dispatch_task

value.description: Send a task of an approved recovery option to an authorized ground team.

items.rationale: The brief asks the system to coordinate authorized teams. Dispatching only follows an approval.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: confirm_task_completion

value.description: Record that a team has completed its dispatched task.

items.rationale: Closing the coordination loop is needed to know when recovery is done.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: close_recovery

value.description: Mark the approved option as executed and the conflict as resolved once its tasks are complete.

items.rationale: A conflict is resolved when the approved recovery has been carried out.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: complete_turnaround

value.description: Close the turnaround once all its conflicts are resolved.

items.rationale: This is the end of a case.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: R1_human_approval_recovery

value.description: Every recovery option is approved by an operations controller, never autonomously by an agent.

items.rationale: Recovery decisions affect crew, passengers, slots and money. They belong to a person.

items.name: R2_safety_authority_review

value.description: A recovery option that affects safety-critical operations must be approved by the competent safety/operational authority.

items.rationale: The brief requires safety-critical operations to remain subject to the appropriate operational authorities.

items.name: R3_no_unapproved_safety_dispatch

value.description: Safety-critical tasks may not be dispatched for an option that has not been approved.

items.rationale: This is a guard on safety-critical operations, in addition to the precondition.

items.name: R4_trace_before_dispatch

value.description: The decision must be recorded in the decision trail before any task is dispatched.

items.rationale: The brief asks for a complete decision trail.

items.name: R5_safety_escalation

value.description: A safety-critical conflict is escalated to the operational authority before recovery options are approved.

items.rationale: This keeps safety-critical matters with the authorities from the start.

items.name: R6_approval_access

value.description: Only operations controllers and safety authorities may approve or reject recovery options.

items.rationale: The brief requires coordination of authorized teams and authority over safety-critical operations.

items.name: R7_rejection_access

value.description: Only operations controllers and safety authorities may reject recovery options.

items.rationale: Rejection needs the same authority as approval.

items.name: R8_dispatch_access

value.description: Only operations controllers may dispatch tasks to ground teams.

items.rationale: Teams act only on instructions from an authorized controller.

items.name: R9_trail_integrity

value.description: Only the deciding roles may write the decision field of the decision trail.

items.rationale: This protects the integrity of the decision trail.

items.name: turnaround_recovered

value.description: The disrupted turnaround is completed, with every conflict resolved through an approved and recorded recovery.

items.rationale: The outcome sought by the brief is controlled recovery of delayed turnarounds.

questions.question: Which operations or task types count as safety-critical (e.g. fuelling, de-icing, pushback, loading/weight & balance), and which authority approves each one (airline, airport, duty manager, regulator)?
questions.why: Rules R2, R3 and R5 depend on the safety_critical flag and on who the safety_authority is.

questions.question: Is there a cost or delay threshold above which a recovery option needs a higher-level approver? What is the amount and who approves?
questions.why: Decisions involving money beyond a stated limit belong to a designated person. No limit is given, so no threshold rule is proposed.

questions.question: May any low-impact recovery option (e.g. swapping equivalent ground equipment) be applied without human approval? If so, under what limits?
questions.why: For now, R1 requires a human approval on every option.

questions.question: Who decides on crew reassignments and slot changes: your operations control, the airline, or the slot coordinator? Is the system only meant to raise these conflicts?
questions.why: This determines whether crew and slot recovery are actions in scope or only escalations.

questions.question: What must the decision trail contain and how long must it be kept (regulatory or contractual requirements)? Who may read it?
questions.why: This sets the DecisionRecord attributes and the data_access rules.

questions.question: Which systems provide flight, crew, equipment and slot data at each airport, and how are teams reached (handheld app, radio dispatch, messaging)?
questions.why: These are needed to describe the integrations and the dispatch capability.

questions.question: Does a turnaround count as completed at off-blocks/departure, or when all its conflicts are resolved?
questions.why: This defines the goal target and the complete_turnaround precondition.

roles.name: operations_controller
roles.description: Ground-handling operations controller who reviews and approves or rejects recovery options and dispatches tasks to teams.

roles.name: safety_authority
roles.description: Competent operational or safety authority (e.g. duty manager or airline/airport authority) who must approve anything affecting safety-critical operations and receives escalations.

roles.name: ground_team_lead
roles.description: Lead of an authorized ground handling team who receives dispatched tasks and confirms their completion.

roles.name: auditor
roles.description: Read-only reviewer of the decision trail for compliance and post-incident analysis.

agents.name: conflict_monitor_agent
agents.description: Watches turnaround progress and operational feeds, registers conflicts and escalates safety-critical or unresolvable ones.

agents.name: recovery_planner_agent
agents.description: Generates and scores recovery alternatives and submits them for human review. It never approves them.

agents.name: coordination_agent
agents.description: Records decisions in the trail, then relays approved tasks to authorized teams and tracks their completion.

integrations.system: Airport operational database / A-CDM feed and airline flight information
integrations.description: Flight schedules, actual times, turnaround milestones and delays per airport.

integrations.system: Resource management system (ground equipment, staff rosters) plus airline crew and connection data
integrations.description: Availability data used to build and score recovery alternatives.
Lets controllers and safety authorities review, approve, reject and receive escalations.

integrations.system: Ground team dispatch / mobile task system
integrations.description: Sends tasks to authorized teams and receives completion confirmations.

suggestions.note: descriptions only: roles are granted and systems are connected by an administrator

assumptions.statement: A case is one turnaround of one flight at one airport. Conflicts spanning several turnarounds (e.g. a shared crew) are handled as separate linked conflicts.
Agents only detect, propose, record and dispatch after approval. No recovery option is applied without a human decision.
Passenger connection and crew conflicts are flagged and coordinated with the airline, not decided by the ground handler.
Severity is a free-text level (e.g. low/medium/high) until a scale is given.

unknowns: The list of safety-critical operations and the competent authority for each
Monetary or delay thresholds for escalation to a higher approver
Response deadlines for approvals relative to scheduled departure
Source systems and data feeds per airport
Retention and access requirements for the decision trail
Contractual service levels with airlines that could constrain recovery options

understanding.summary: A ground-handling company working across several airports wants a system that detects operational conflicts during aircraft turnarounds, evaluates recovery alternatives, coordinates authorized teams and keeps a complete decision trail. Conflicts can involve crew, passenger connections, ground equipment, servicing tasks or departure slots. Safety-critical operations stay with the appropriate operational authorities. understanding.outcome: Each disrupted turnaround is brought to completion through a recovery option approved by an authorized person. Every decision is recorded, and safety-critical changes are approved by the competent operational authority.
actors: Safety / operational authorities responsible for safety-critical operations
out_of_scope: Crew duty-time legality decisions and crew rostering itself (owned by the airlines; only flagged as conflicts)
Passenger rebooking, compensation and passenger-rights handling
Negotiating or reallocating departure slots with the slot coordinator (only requests are coordinated)
Billing and invoicing of ground-handling services
